Location: Onsite - Burnet, TX

Employment Type: Direct Hire, Full-Time

Job Title: Test Facility Manager

 

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"-we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge-on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

 

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month-not next year-this is your playground.

 

Position Summary

We are hiring a Test Facility Manager to run our test facility at Reveille Peak Ranch in Burnet, Texas, and lead the 9 Mothers team based there. Everything we build is proven at this site: belt-fed shotgun systems, robotic turrets, and the tracking algorithms that aim them, fired live against low-flying drones. It is a live-fire range with robotic weapons and UAS operating together, about an hour from Austin. You own it: the people, the ground, the buildings, the weapons and ammunition on site, and the budget.

You also own test execution, as a senior engineer. Engineers in Austin will write most of the test plans, and you are their peer: you review every plan for what can actually be executed and measured, push back when it will not produce a decision-quality result, and write plans yourself when needed. On test day you execute the plan expertly, from site preparation through the pre-test brief, the hold and abort calls, the as-run record, and the data that leaves the range. We make engineering decisions from that data. If a test leaves it ambiguous, that is on you, regardless of who wrote the plan.

Safety comes first. Test days may bring engineers from Austin, customers, and distinguished visitors who have never stood behind a hot gun line, and you are responsible for every one of them. You function as Range Safety Officer whenever no other qualified RSO is present and hold cease-fire authority over everything on the site.

We run 5 to 10 test days a month today and are moving toward daily testing. Getting there means building the infrastructure, procedures, and team that can sustain that cadence without safety or data standards slipping, and there is real potential for this role to grow with the team.

This is a hands-on role in the most literal sense. There is no crew at the ranch but the one you lead. You will set targets, repair firing positions, run generators, pull cable, fix what breaks, and police brass alongside your technicians. If you expect to manage a range from an office, this is not the job.

Without this team doing its job, our life-saving defensive systems never make it to the battlefield.

 

What You'll Do

- Run the site. Own day-to-day operation: buildings, range infrastructure (firing positions, berms, targets, surface danger zones, UAS operating area), power, comms, vehicles, equipment, and the budget that pays for them. Keep it maintained, secured, and ready to test.

- Lead the team at the ranch. Hire, train, schedule, and manage the technicians and range hands at the site. Set the standard for how work gets done and hold the team to it. You are the senior 9 Mothers presence on site.

- Execute test campaigns. Turn engineering's test plans into safe, productive test days: site preparation, test article and instrumentation setup, the pre-test brief and go/no-go, the sequence of events, hold and abort decisions, and the post-test debrief.

- Engineer the measurement. Own instrumentation and data acquisition at the sit

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

title: Agrotechnical Director
description:
RAW Ventures is Hiring for Fermata
Fermata, one of RAW Ventures’ portfolio companies, is an AgTech innovator using computer vision and AI to detect plant diseases and pests early, helping growers reduce losses and optimize yields.
Learn more at fermata.tech.
The opportunity
Fermata is hiring a senior agronomist and agtech leader to own the direction of our
agrotechnical development and to be the person who knows where growers' pain and
money are, and which problems are worth solving. Y ou will be Fermata's senior authority
on agronomy and crop protection, accountable for the agronomic quality of everything
Fermata delivers.
About Fermata
Fermata is an agtech company delivering digital scouting and agronomic decision support
to commercial growers, propagators, nurseries and seed producers. Its Croptimus
platform combines optical zoom cameras with computer vision to monitor crops daily and
detect early signs of more than 20 types of pests, diseases and other plant issues.
Fermata has customers in Canada, the Netherlands, Greece, the United Kingdom and
other markets.
Key responsibilities
Agrotechnical direction and customer value

• Own the direction of agrotechnical development: which crops, pests, growing systems (greenhouse, nursery, propagation, outdoor) and capabilities Fermata should develop next, and in what order.

• Be the company's source of truth on what growers find useful or essential, where their biggest pain and costs are, and what they will pay for.

• Act as consultant and early-stage hypothesis validator for the Product Lead and the Sales Director: test ideas against real grower practice and identify the segments, crops and use cases with the strongest value.

• Translate greenhouse economics - yield, labour, crop-protection and energy costs, crop-loss impact - into value cases and ROI arguments.

Agronomic quality and pilots

• Own the agronomic logic and content behind Croptimus: thresholds, recommended
actions, pest and disease libraries and treatment guidance.

• Work with the ML team on ground truth and labelling standards; validate and sign off
detection models and new detection classes.

• Define pilot methodology and success criteria, analyse results and produce case
studies that prove customer value.
Growers, industry and team

• Act as senior agronomic advisor to strategic customers: keep an ongoing dialogue
with head growers, IPM managers, agronomists and agrotechnologists, and join sales
meetings as the internal agronomic expert when needed.

• Use and grow relationships with grower cooperatives, associations, biological-control
and crop-protection companies; represent Fermata at industry events.
Design agronomic training for customers and customer-facing teams, and build and
lead the agronomy function.
How this role works with others
The Managing Director owns strategy and major trade-offs; the Product Lead owns the
product vision, roadmap and requirements; the Sales Director owns new-customer
acquisition, proposals, pricing and negotiations; the Operations Director owns customer
success, installations, the project portfolio and R&D partnerships; ML and Engineering
own models and architecture.
Measures of success

• Product and commercial priorities are based on clear agronomic and economic
evidence of what customers need and will pay for.

• Detections and recommendations are agronomically accurate and trusted by growers;
pilots produce clear evidence for rollout decisions.

• Documented customer value in priority accounts: earlier detection, lower crop loss,
optimised treatments or scouting-labour savings.

• Customers, cooperatives and industry partners recognise Fermata as a credible
agronomic expert.
Required experience and capabilities

• Degree in agronomy, horticulture, plant protection or a related agrotechnical field.

• Substantial hands-on experience in commercial greenhouse production and outdoor cultivation, including scouting, IPM and biological and chemical control.

• Crop expertise
